title: Earthworks progress report
draft: DRAFT — includes results that have not been released
demoNotice: Demonstration resolution. This report uses elevation data at {resolution} m per pixel (typical of ASTER and Copernicus GLO-30). It shows the workflow only; real earthworks measurement needs sub-metre satellite stereo or drone surveys.
summaryLead: Between the baseline survey of {baseline_date} and the survey of {survey_date}, the measured change over the whole site is:
summaryBaseline: This is the baseline survey of the site. Volumes and progress are measured from it, so there is no earlier survey to compare it with.
summaryNoAnalysis: The comparison with the baseline has not been computed yet, so no volumes are shown.
noDesign: No design surface is available for this site, so progress is not reported.
mapTerrain: Terrain at the survey date (shaded relief)
scaleBar: The bar in the corner is {length} m long. North is up.
legendRamp: Height change: −{range} m (cut) to +{range} m (fill). Changes smaller than {lod} m are not drawn.
tableNote: ± ranges are {confidence}% confidence intervals. Height changes smaller than {lod} m are not counted. Height error used: {pixel} m per pixel and {systematic} m systematic, {source}.

source.stable_ground: measured on stable ground outside the zones
source.stated_accuracy: taken from the surveys' stated accuracy
source.alignment_residual: taken from the survey's alignment to the baseline

coverageWarning: Elevation data covers only {percent}% of “{name}”; its volumes are incomplete.
stale: Zones, alignment or settings changed after this result was computed; it should be recomputed.
chartNote: Progress per zone = volume achieved since the baseline ÷ volume the design requires. Bars show the ± range. The dashed line is 100 %; the vertical line marks this report's survey.
methodP1: Each survey is an elevation model of the site. Surveys are placed on a common metric grid (UTM zone, EPSG:{epsg}) and in one height reference, then aligned to the baseline survey using ground outside the work zones, which should not have changed.
methodP2: The height change is the later surface minus the earlier one, pixel by pixel. Fill is the sum of height increases × pixel area, cut the sum of decreases, and net is fill − cut. A pixel belongs to a zone when its centre is inside the zone outline.
methodP3: Changes too small to tell apart from measurement noise (the level of detection) are not counted. The ± range combines pixel noise, which partly averages out over an area, with systematic error, which does not, and an allowance for noise that exceeds the level of detection.
methodP4: These figures measure the change of the surface. They do not account for compaction, bulking or settlement, and a surface model includes whatever stands on the ground. The full method is described in METHOD.md supplied with the system.
alignShift: Vertical shift {offset} m; residual RMSE {rmse} m
align3d: Moved {north} m N, {east} m E; then {text}
